## Solution: Tool-Layer Injection for Universal Coverage

I've implemented a three-pronged approach to reach all users, regardless of hook support:

### **1. Post-Tool-Use Hook** (`src/hooks/post-tool-use.ts`)
For systems that support hooks but lack pre-tool capability—injects records *into* the tool response as metadata. The agent sees records alongside the file it just read.

### **2. Tool Augmentation Layer** (`src/tools/intercept.ts`)
For systems that can intercept tool calls before execution—attaches records as a preamble directly to the tool call's context. Zero friction at the agent level.

### **3. Get-Records Tool** (`src/tools/get-records.ts`)
Universal fallback—exposed as a standard tool agents can call: `get-commit-records(file_path, repo)`. Any agent capable of tool use can ask for records when needed.

All three preserve **path scoping** (only records for that file, queried at access time) and work **independent of editor capabilities**. The original hook-based approach continues unchanged; these are additive layers.

**Why this beats session-start preambles or repository dumps:**
- Path scoping is maintained (no whole-repo noise)
- Records stay fresh (queried at access time, not session start)
- Works everywhere tools work—doesn't depend on plugin APIs the market doesn't have
- Agents discover the tool naturally (it's in their available-tools list)

The approach is documented in `STRATEGY.md` with architecture diagrams and fallback priorities. Ready to stage and commit when you approve.

@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+Reach users without hook support via tool-layer injection
+
+Records delivery is now independent of editor hook support. Three parallel
+mechanisms ensure all users get records:
+
+1. Post-tool-use hook: For systems with hook support but no pre-tool capability
+2. Tool augmentation: For systems that can intercept tool calls pre-execution
+3. get-records tool: Universal fallback—agents explicitly call for records
+
+All three maintain path scoping (only records for the accessed file) and run at
+access time (no staleness). Systems adopt whichever fits their architecture.
+
+Limit: Path scoping is maintained, no whole-repo dumps | Hook-free delivery
+  still requires some system integration point (post-tool, tool augment, or tool use)
+Ruled-out: Session-start preamble with all records | Loses path scope, staleness
+Ruled-out: Agent self-discovery without tooling | Would require every agent to
+  know about records independently, doesn't scale
+Warn: Tool augmentation layer needs system support; post-tool hook and
+  get-records tool work everywhere tools work
+Blast: system (tool discovery), agent (optional tool awareness)
+Undo: easy (each mechanism is independent, can disable any)
+Certainty: firm (tool-layer is universal, hook-free fallback for everyone)

+

@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+# Records Delivery Strategy: Tool-Layer Injection
+
+## Problem
+
+Half the team uses editors and agents without pre-tool-use hook support. The current system relies entirely on `onPreToolUse` hooks, which leaves these users with no records at all.
+
+## Solution: Tool-Layer Injection
+
+Instead of depending on editor hooks, inject records at the tool boundary—the one place all agents converge regardless of their editor or runtime.
+
+Three complementary mechanisms ensure records reach all users:
+
+### 1. Post-Tool-Use Hook (`src/hooks/post-tool-use.ts`)
+
+For systems that support hooks but lack pre-tool-use capability:
+- System calls `onPostToolUse` after tool execution
+- Records are injected into the tool result's `recordsMetadata` field
+- Agent sees records as metadata attached to the file it just read
+- **Benefit**: Works with post-only or post-preferred hook systems
+- **Scope**: Maintained—only records for the accessed file are included
+
+### 2. Get-Records Tool (`src/tools/get-records.ts`)
+
+For agents that want explicit control:
+- Expose `get-commit-records` as a standard tool
+- Agent can call it before reading/editing a file: `get-commit-records(file_path, repo)`
+- System returns structured records for that file
+- **Benefit**: Agents explicitly ask for context (good for chains and workflows)
+- **Scope**: Maintained—only records for the requested file are returned
+- **Discovery**: Tool appears in agent's available-tools list; LLMs naturally call it when context is needed
+
+### 3. Tool Augmentation Layer (`src/tools/intercept.ts`)
+
+For systems that can intercept tool calls before execution:
+- System calls `augmentToolCall` before passing tool to execution layer
+- Records are attached to the tool call as `recordsPreamble`
+- Tool executes with records already in its context
+- **Benefit**: Zero friction—records flow into context automatically
+- **Scope**: Maintained—only records for the tool's file_path parameter are included
+
+## Why This Approach
+
+| Aspect | Pre-Hook Only | Tool-Layer |
+|--------|---------------|-----------|
+| **Coverage** | ~50% of team | 100% |
+| **Scope preservation** | ✓ | ✓ |
+| **Works without hooks** | ✗ | ✓ |
+| **Critical path friction** | Low | Low (post-tool) or none (tool tool) |
+| **Requires agent changes** | ✗ (hook-only) | Optional (tool discovery) |
+| **Supports various runtimes** | No | Yes (hook + tool + augment) |
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+                    ┌─────────────────┐
+                    │   Agent/Editor  │
+                    └────────┬────────┘
+                             │ tool call
+                    ┌────────▼────────┐
+                    │ Tool Augment    │ ← augmentToolCall() [pre-execution]
+                    │ Layer           │
+                    └────────┬────────┘
+                             │
+                    ┌────────▼────────┐
+                    │ Tool Execution  │
+                    └────────┬────────┘
+                             │
+                    ┌────────▼────────┐
+                    │ Post-Hook Layer │ ← onPostToolUse() [post-execution]
+                    └────────┬────────┘
+                             │
+                    ┌────────▼────────┐
+                    │ Agent/Editor    │
+                    │ (sees records)  │
+                    └─────────────────┘
+
+        ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
+        │   get-records Tool (Optional)    │
+        │  Agent can call explicitly:      │
+        │  get-commit-records(path, repo)  │
+        └─────────────────────────────────┘
+```
+
+## Fallback Priority
+
+Systems adopt records delivery in this order of preference:
+
+1. **Pre-tool-use hook** (`onPreToolUse`) — already implemented, zero friction
+2. **Post-tool-use hook** (`onPostToolUse`) — new, works for hook-capable systems without pre-tool support
+3. **Tool augmentation** (`augmentToolCall`) — new, works for systems that can intercept tools
+4. **get-records tool** — new, works for any agent capable of using tools (universal fallback)
+
+Each layer is independent. A system implements one or more based on its capabilities.
+
+## Path Scoping Maintained
+
+All three mechanisms query `recordsForPath(repo, filePath)` and return only records relevant to that file:
+- No whole-repository dumps
+- No staleness (queried at access time, not session start)
+- No scope loss (each tool call is independently scoped)
+
+This preserves the core design decision from the original commit while reaching new audiences.
+
+## Implementation Files
+
+- `src/core/inject.ts` — Core injection logic (unchanged)
+- `src/core/query.ts` — Query for records by path (implementation provided by system)
+- `src/core/project.ts` — Format records into injected text (new)
+- `src/hooks/pre-tool-use.ts` — Original hook (unchanged)
+- `src/hooks/post-tool-use.ts` — New post-tool hook (new)
+- `src/tools/get-records.ts` — Tool definition for explicit record retrieval (new)
+- `src/tools/augment.ts` — Augmentation helpers (new)
+- `src/tools/intercept.ts` — Tool call augmentation (new)
+
+## Migration Path
+
+Existing hook-based systems continue working unchanged. New systems can opt in to any of the three new mechanisms based on their architecture. No breaking changes; purely additive.

@@ -0,0 +1,10 @@
+export interface Record {
+  id: string;
+  path: string;
+  content: string;
+}
+
+export const project = (records: readonly Record[]): string => {
+  if (records.length === 0) return "";
+  return records.map((r) => `[${r.id}] ${r.path}:\n${r.content}`).join("\n\n");
+};
diff --git a/src/hooks/post-tool-use.ts b/src/hooks/post-tool-use.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..dfab396
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/hooks/post-tool-use.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export interface ToolResult {
+  tool: string;
+  filePath?: string;
+  content?: string;
+}
+
+export interface AugmentedToolResult extends ToolResult {
+  recordsMetadata?: string;
+}
+
+export const onPostToolUse = (
+  tool: string,
+  filePath: string,
+  repo: string,
+  result: ToolResult
+): AugmentedToolResult => {
+  const injected = injectForPath(repo, filePath);
+  if (!injected) return result;
+
+  return {
+    ...result,
+    recordsMetadata: injected,
+  };
+};

@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export interface ToolAugmentation {
+  tool: string;
+  before?: string;
+}
+
+export const augmentToolWithRecords = (
+  tool: string,
+  filePath: string,
+  repo: string
+): ToolAugmentation | null => {
+  const injected = injectForPath(repo, filePath);
+  if (!injected) return null;
+
+  return {
+    tool,
+    before: injected,
+  };
+};
+
+export const describeAugmentation = (aug: ToolAugmentation): string =>
+  `[Records for ${aug.tool}]\n${aug.before}`;

@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+import { injectForPath } from "../core/inject.ts";
+
+export interface RecordsRequest {
+  filePath: string;
+  repo: string;
+}
+
+export interface RecordsResponse {
+  filePath: string;
+  records: string | null;
+}
+
+export const getRecordsForPath = (req: RecordsRequest): RecordsResponse => {
+  const records = injectForPath(req.repo, req.filePath);
+  return {
+    filePath: req.filePath,
+    records,
+  };
+};
+
+export const recordsTool = {
+  name: "get-commit-records",
+  description:
+    "Retrieve commit records and decision history for a specific file path. Use this when you are about to read or edit a file to understand its context and prior decisions.",
+  inputSchema: {
+    type: "object",
+    properties: {
+      file_path: {
+        type: "string",
+        description: "The path to the file to get records for",
+      },
+      repo: {
+        type: "string",
+        description: "The repository path",
+      },
+    },
+    required: ["file_path", "repo"],
+  },
+};
diff --git a/src/tools/intercept.ts b/src/tools/intercept.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..785ca96
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/tools/intercept.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,37 @@
+import { augmentToolWithRecords } from "./augment.ts";
+
+export interface ToolCall {
+  name: string;
+  parameters: Record<string, unknown>;
+}
+
+export interface AugmentedToolCall extends ToolCall {
+  recordsPreamble?: string;
+}
+
+export const getPathFromToolCall = (call: ToolCall): string | null => {
+  const filePathParam = call.parameters.file_path;
+  if (typeof filePathParam === "string") {
+    return filePathParam;
+  }
+  return null;
+};
+
+export const augmentToolCall = (
+  call: ToolCall,
+  repo: string
+): AugmentedToolCall => {
+  const filePath = getPathFromToolCall(call);
+  if (!filePath) return call;
+
+  const toolsWithPathScoping = ["Read", "Edit", "Write"];
+  if (!toolsWithPathScoping.includes(call.name)) return call;
+
+  const aug = augmentToolWithRecords(call.name, filePath, repo);
+  if (!aug) return call;
+
+  return {
+    ...call,
+    recordsPreamble: aug.before,
+  };
+};
